lines.Dunn the Deserter: The Wither. The actual Wither. The camps used to scare recruits with stories of it.
lines.Corwin the Refugee: My children won't believe this. I barely do.
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: Its blood was black. I'm glad I didn't want it.

lines.Dunn the Deserter: A dragon. If my old captain could see me now.
lines.Corwin the Refugee: I farmed turnips a year ago.
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: Everyone's dreaming of a headless king. Me too.

lines.Dunn the Deserter: Seven. Something's wrong. It's too quiet.
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: I can feel something waking up. Like hunger.

lines.Dunn the Deserter: The old woman lied to you for years. I know what that's like, from the other side.
lines.Corwin the Refugee: She sent you letters every week. Liars don't usually bother.
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: She's older than she looks. A lot older.

lines.Dunn the Deserter: Whatever you decide in there, I'm still behind you.
lines.Corwin the Refugee: Come back. That's all. Just come back.
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: He offered you something, didn't he? I know that look.

lines.Dunn the Deserter: It's over. I don't know what to do with my hands.
lines.Corwin the Refugee: I'm going to plant something. Anything. Just to watch it grow.
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: Thank you. For all of it. For sitting with me.

lines.Dunn the Deserter: You knelt. I ran from men like you once. I'm too tired to run again.
lines.Corwin the Refugee: ...I'll stay. Someone has to remember who you were.
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: Now you're the one with the hunger.

lines.Dunn the Deserter: He was just a boy with a sick friend.
lines.Corwin the Refugee: I stole grain to feed my children. What was that for?
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: I know that look. I wore it for two years.

lines.Dunn the Deserter: You walked away from the camp too. Welcome to the club.
lines.Ansel the Blood-Drinker: Getting clean is the hardest thing. You did it.
